primary_endpoint: Random-direction response NRMSE at b=3 paired records per actuator per round, averaged equally over twelve rounds, eight sequences, four schedules and four measurement-noise levels, then over networks within each fixed task and over tasks.
selection: Select memory ratio on five development checkpoints only. Independently select a window, a decay, and a hazard/likelihood-strength pair, then select the strongest baseline family by the same development endpoint. Lock choices and hashes before any confirmation evaluation. Retain the complete grid.
memory_rule: Same binary actuator entries and loss-ratio acceptance rule as the existing experiment. Compare replacing each incumbent sign with its opposite using current-round losses; keep unaccepted entries. No neural weights are updated.
baselines: Roundwise matched-prior loss minimization; windowed historical matched-prior loss minimization; exponentially discounted losses; a factorized two-state Markov filter with a tuned symmetric transition hazard and source-calibrated composite likelihood. All baselines retain past information and have the same binary hypothesis class and source-only coordinate weights.
ablations: Frozen source map, default ratio 0.5, gate removed (ratio 1), and memory reset to the source map before each round. Include a true-map reference, not an oracle control return.
schedules_definition: All maps start at +1. Stationary never changes. Sparse toggles one randomly selected actuator at each change round. Dense toggles ceil(d/2) randomly selected actuators. Recurrent alternates the source and one random ceil(d/2)-flipped map in three-round blocks. The estimator receives no schedule, change time, noise level, true map or test answer.
information_budget: Every estimator receives exactly the same noisy paired intervention responses in each round, the same source fit and initial source map, and all previous rounds. Each round queries every actuator b times. Evaluation responses are separate and never enter updates. Hyperparameter search has five memory choices and 23 baseline choices, favoring the baseline search rather than restricting it.
physical_protocol: Fresh physical states from each frozen actor, source/validation/adaptation/test splits with disjoint hashes. Axis-aligned contrasts under a sign remapping change sign exactly; this algebraic identity is checked against additional direct simulator calls. Random-direction test responses are simulated for all sign maps (using the exact global-reversal symmetry). This is intervention-response adaptation, not end-to-end return optimization.
noise_model: Independent Gaussian measurement noise scaled coordinatewise by source-training response RMS. The same draws are reused across methods, budgets and schedules. Source-only inverse-energy weighting is supplied to every method. Noise levels are not passed to estimators.
checkpoint_scope: One development and two confirmation checkpoints per task, all existing independently trained released networks used in prior work. New collection and split seeds. Confirmation is held out for this study's selection, not a claim of previously unseen networks.
inference: Paired checkpoint bootstrap within each of the five fixed tasks, after averaging sequences and rounds. Do not count rounds, queries or noise draws as independent trained agents. Report all schedules, noise levels, budgets and losses of advantage. No outcome-dependent stopping or test-set tuning.
